title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind arrives free on YouTube to study its legacy
excerpt: Close Encounters of the Third Kind, Spielberg's 1977 classic, can now be watched free on YouTube. The plot follows Roy Neary and Jillian Guiler after they sight UFOs, while a scientific investigation converges on Devils Tower.
content:
The sci-fi classic that Steven Spielberg directed in 1977 can be watched for free on YouTube according to ScreenRant. The film follows Roy Neary, an Indiana utility worker whose life changes after sighting a UFO, and Jillian Guiler, who searches for her son after a similar encounter, while a scientific investigation converges on Devils Tower.

Practical effects and sound design that set a precedent 🎬

Eight Oscar nominations and the award for best cinematography for Vilmos Zsigmond consolidated its legacy. The film remains a reference in the design of practical visual effects and in building tension through light and sound, with the collaboration of Douglas Trumbull and John Williams's five-note musical motif. Its staging of the mothership continues to be studied as an example of analog spectacle prior to the digital era.

Five notes that get stuck in your head more than a summer song 🎵

Now that the film is free on YouTube, anyone can verify that John Williams's famous five-note motif lodges itself in the brain as easily as the chorus of a commercial song. The difference is that here the result is art and not an auditory torment. New artists and filmmakers have direct access to this visual language without paying admission, something worth taking advantage of before someone decides to put a price on it again.
